# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented here. The format follows
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and this project
adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [3.0.3] - 2026-11-13

A role for a group that should see only some sections, and See all reports for those of them who see the whole
organization. Everything in 3.0.2 is included.

**Install over 3.0.2 (or 3.0.1):** disable the nightly task, replace the scripts on the job server with this release's
(keep `copilot-audit.settings.psd1` and `logs`), and run `.\Install-CopilotAudit.ps1 -SqlServer <server> -Dashboard`
once: it widens the role checks on `dash.RoleGrant` and `dash.AccessProfileRole` to take the new role, and nothing
already granted changes. Enable the task again. Then deploy the dashboard from `copilot-insights-v3.0.3.zip` with
`dashboard\Install-CopilotInsights.ps1 -PackagePath` on each web server; it keeps the site's settings. The Workbench's
worker has no change. From 3.0.1, the 3.0.2 notes below apply as well.

### Added
- **The Restricted role,** for a group that should see only some sections. It narrows instead of opening: its holder
  sees Start, Leadership and the sections their other roles open, and nothing else. *Restricted* with *Agents* is Start,
  Leadership and Agents. Regions, People, App owners and Governance, which belong to no role, and the Workbench (unless
  they also hold a Workbench role or Admin) are gone from their menu, start page and links, and refused at their address
  with a page that says why. It never lets anyone past the dashboard's level limit on its own, widens nothing, and
  changes nothing for anyone who does not hold it. Admin › Access, access profiles and `-Task GrantRole` offer it.
  docs\OPERATIONS.md, *A group that sees only some sections*.
- **See all reports,** for a restricted person who sees the whole organization (the Organization role, level 1 or 2, or
  a persona role granted across the whole organization): under Start in the menu, it lifts the restriction for them
  until they choose *Show only my reports*. It never opens a section whose role they lack; each switch is audited; a
  cookie set by anyone else changes nothing.

### Changed
- **A review of the change** before release: the daily pre-cache's stand-in viewer, which holds every role, would have
  held Restricted too and skipped the unguarded sections (it leaves Restricted out); the seat figures on Leadership ›
  Copilot reservations and Licensing › Reservation holders linked a restricted viewer to Workbench pages they would be
  refused (no links for them now).

### Known limits
- The data API's aggregate calls (`usage`, `units`, `value`, `targets`) are Leadership's figures and stay open to a
  restricted viewer; Power BI and the emailed digests are not narrowed by the role.

## [3.0.2] - 2026-11-12

A fix release: the nightly load keeps loading when Microsoft marks audit searches failed that still have their
records, two settings for slow audit searches, and the side menu working again where a build server re-encoded the
scripts.

**Install over 3.0.1:** no schema change and no new setting is required. Disable the nightly task, replace the scripts
on the job server with this release's (keep `copilot-audit.settings.psd1` and `logs`), and enable the task again.
Deploy the dashboard from this release's `copilot-insights-v3.0.2.zip` with `dashboard\Install-CopilotInsights.ps1
-PackagePath` on each web server; it keeps the site's settings. The Workbench's worker has no change: leaving it at 3.0.1 is fine.
`Install-CopilotAudit.ps1` need not be run.

### Fixed
- **Purview searches marked failed that still have their records.** Since November 2026 some tenants' audit searches
  end `failed` although they found records, and the records still download. The loader retried and split such a
  window until it was written off, so nothing loaded for days. A failed search that reports records is now taken as
  complete and loaded (one over the record cap is split as usual), with a warning in the log. A search that failed
  with no records is retried as before, and the log and the window's `LastError` now carry Microsoft's whole answer.
- **The menu stopped folding when the scripts were re-encoded.** A copy of the source that reached a build server in
  another encoding turned a character in a regular expression of `site.js` into one the browser refused, and the
  whole script stopped on every page. The scripts now write such characters as `\u` escapes, and a test keeps their
  code plain ASCII.
- **`/workbench` on its own** was a page not found; it now opens the Workbench's Start page.

### Added
- **Audit search settings for the nightly run.** `AuditSearchTimeoutMinutes` (how long a search may run before it
  is submitted again, 240 by default) and `AuditSearchesInFlight` (8 by default) in the settings file reach every
  Purview load. The loader takes `-QueryTimeoutMinutes`. A value out of range (30 to 1440 minutes; 1 to 40 searches)
  stops the run at its start and names the setting, rather than failing the load's parameters. docs\OPERATIONS.md,
  *The pipeline*.

### Changed
- **An adversarial review of 3.0.2** found five issues, fixed before release with tests:
  - a search Microsoft marked failed that reported records but then refused to serve them (HTTP 400 or 403) stopped
    the whole load as a fatal error; such a window is now searched again, as a failed search was before;
  - a window loaded from a failed search left no trace once loaded; its `LastError` now keeps
    `loaded from a search Microsoft marked failed: ~N records reported, M loaded`, and the log warns when under 90% of
    the reported records loaded, with how to load those hours again (RUNBOOK section 8);
  - the log said *treating it as complete* for a failed search over the record cap, which is in fact split;
  - the two search settings were not described outside the runbook, and a value out of range failed the load with a
    parameter error that did not name the setting;
  - a test of the history run's steps (`tests\Test-Provisioning.ps1`) had been joined to the line before it and no
    longer ran.

## [3.0.1] - 2026-11-02

The rest of the 3.0.0 plan: one rule set for Copilot seats, Copilot Credits charged to the Workbench's lines of
business, a reporting view, and Finance's open seat questions as settings, so they no longer hold anything up.

**Install over 3.0.0:** rerun `Install-CopilotInsights.ps1 -GovernanceDatabase <name>` (with `-GrantDatabaseAccess`,
or the printed command for a DBA) so the Workbench database gets the new view and settings, and deploy the dashboard
and the worker from this release. No new package. Nothing changes where the Workbench is off.

### Added
- **One purchase gate and one seat rule set.** The purchase gate is one rule (`SeatPolicy.PurchaseGate`) for the
  Workbench and for Insights' leader-based register, with its share and baseline as seat settings
  (`Seats.PurchaseGatePercent`, 95; `Seats.GateBaselineUnassigned`). Leadership › Copilot reservations and Ownership
  registry › Copilot seats say the same gate, true-down and Finance sentences.
- **Finance's open seat choices are settings,** each with its default named on the pages: who pays for seats no line
  of business claims (`Seats.NoLobChargedTo`: a funding owner's code; empty, as before, a row of their own charged to
  no line of business), the rate per seat (`Seats.RatePerSeatMonth`, a placeholder) and when an increase takes effect
  (`Seats.IncreaseEffective`). The monthly draft charges no-LOB seats to the active funding owner named, as seats
  above its reservation (a row of its own when it has none); a code that names no active funding owner leaves them a
  row of their own, and the pages say so.
- **`rpt.vSeatReservationCurrent`** in the Workbench database: today's seats by line of business with the latest
  certified month's chargeback (one month for every row, so its amounts add up), for Power BI and Grafana through its
  reporting role, `gov_reader`.
- **`dash.LineOfBusinessName`** in the Copilot database: the Workbench's funding owners' codes and names, kept by the
  dashboard every quarter hour, so a month's credit snapshot keeps the names it had.

### Changed
- **Leadership › Credit chargeback,** with the Workbench on, charges each environment's credits to a Workbench funding
  owner: a route's Org ID is the funding owner's code, its name comes from there, a viewer of part of the organization
  sees the lines the Workbench's seat scope gives them, and an agent is misrouted when its environment's line is not the one
  whose tracking group holds its owner's seat. Off, it keeps the reservation register.
- **One person list.** The worker's directory read gives a person recorded without an Entra object ID the one
  Insights records for the same UPN: an enabled account with one object ID for it, and only if no other person here
  has it.
- **An adversarial review of 3.0.1** found 12 issues, fixed before release with tests: the tenant-wide gate shown to
  a viewer of one line of business, a no-LOB charge the pages promised but the draft did not make, the view mixing
  months, a credit viewer's lines not matching their seat scope, old wording, codes and setting names shown to
  non-administrators, snapshot names, the person link's cost and a reused UPN, uncached reads and a failed page when
  the Workbench database does not answer, and "1,136" read as no baseline.
- **`Test-FigureLinks.ps1 -ActAs`** checks the seat figures that open Workbench pages, as a test persona.

### Known limits
- As in 3.0.0, apart from the seat questions, which are now settings.

## [3.0.0] - 2026-11-02

Copilot Insights and the Governance Workbench are one product. The Workbench, where requests for Copilot workloads are
approved by the RACI matrix, funding owners, workloads, envelopes and Copilot seats are kept, and consumption events,
drift, recertification, exceptions and retirement are followed, is served by the dashboard under `/workbench`, in its
menu and its look, with the dashboard's sign-in and roles. It keeps its own database, with tamper-evident ledger tables
and row-level security, and a worker that runs as a Windows service. It is off until set up: a site that sets nothing
new works as 2.8.0 did, and the data Insights already holds is not moved or changed.

**Install over 2.8.0:** run `Install-CopilotAudit.ps1 -Dashboard` on the job server (role checks widened, one setting
added, all additive), then build and deploy the dashboard from this release on each web server (docs\BUILD-FROM-SOURCE.md).
The build needs these packages in the feed it uses, new in this release or at a new version:
`Microsoft.Data.SqlClient` 7.1.1, `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience` 10.11.0, `Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting` and
`Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting.WindowsServices` 10.0.14, and `Microsoft.Extensions.Http`, `.Options`,
`.Options.ConfigurationExtensions`, `.Configuration.Abstractions`, `.DependencyInjection.Abstractions` and
`.Logging.Abstractions` 10.0.14, with what they bring in. To turn the Workbench on, follow docs\DEPLOYMENT.md step 27:
`Install-CopilotInsights.ps1 -GovernanceDatabase CopilotGovernance` on every web server, and `-WorkerServer
-WorkerAccount` on one. It needs SQL Server 2022 or later for its database (the installer checks), a gMSA for the
worker, and the worker's app registration (governance\deploy\Deploy-Production.md).

### Added
- **The Governance Workbench, under `/workbench`.** Its 50 pages in five sections of the dashboard's menu: Ownership and
  approvals (start, my work, requests, a consumption problem, recertification, exceptions, retirement), Approval
  queues, Ownership registry (funding owners, workloads, envelopes, Copilot seats, services, control templates, cost
  centers, commercial, discovery), Governance operations (consumption events, drift and findings, sync and freshness,
  attestations, KPIs, the audit trail, seat chargeback) and Workbench settings (RACI, workflows, SLAs and escalation,
  notifications, Workbench roles, seat groups, integrations, the intake switch, wording). Every field has its (i) help;
  a refused page says why and who grants it. docs\GOVERNANCE-USER-GUIDE.md, docs\DASHBOARD.md.
- **Three roles for it in Admin › Access:** Governance (the central pages), GovernanceOperator (and the operator
  pages) and GovernanceAuditor (reports and the audit trail, read only); Admin opens its settings. They show no usage
  data, never pass the dashboard's level limit and never widen to the whole organization. Three starter access
  profiles: Governance team, Governance operator and Governance auditor. The work people do there (RACI positions,
  line-of-business seat admins, delegations) is still given in the Workbench. *Check someone's access* shows both.
- **Its worker as a Windows service** on one server (`-WorkerServer`), its ten jobs each under a SQL lock, and a daily
  ledger digest task. A release asset of its own: `copilot-governance-worker-vX.Y.Z.zip`, with its checksum.
- **One Copilot seat record.** With the Workbench on, Leadership › Copilot reservations and Licensing › Reservation
  holders show its seats by line of business (`core.SeatReservation`), each figure opening the Workbench page with the
  same number. Insights' own register (`dash.Reservation`, its rate and snapshots) keeps every row and column but is no
  longer edited, and the nightly snapshot adds nothing to it (`dash.Setting` *SeatModel*). Workbench settings › Seat
  groups offers its rows once, as each line of business's first reservation, for the FinOps lead to confirm.
- **Seat activity from Insights.** The seat read takes each person's last Copilot use from Insights' records
  (`dash.UserDay`) when it can read the Insights database, so inactive seats are judged on every loaded day and names
  are never hidden; otherwise, or when Insights' data is more than three days old, it reads Microsoft's usage report.
- **Housekeeping in the worker:** a daily retention job keeps 180 days of job runs and deliveries
  (`Retention.WorkerRecordDays`, at least 30), each job's last run and last success always; processed notices keep
  only their key, so a recurring notice is not sent twice. Ledger and audit tables are never touched.
- **A schema baseline for the Workbench database** (`tests\schema-baseline-governance.tsv`): from 3.0.0 it follows the
  same rule as the Copilot database, additive only.
- docs\GOVERNANCE-USER-GUIDE.md, GOVERNANCE-RUNBOOK.md, GOVERNANCE-DECISIONS.md, GOVERNANCE-TEST-ENVIRONMENT.md, and a
  Governance Workbench section in OPERATIONS.md, DASHBOARD.md, DEPLOYMENT.md (step 27) and SCHEMA.md.

### Changed
- `Install-CopilotInsights.ps1` supports `-WhatIf`, and takes `-GovernanceDatabase`, `-SiteUrl`, `-WorkerAccount`,
  `-WorkerServer`, `-WorkerPackagePath`, `-WorkerSettingsFile`, `-WorkerPath`, `-LedgerDigestPath`, `-LedgerDigestAt` and
  `-ProxyUrl`; without them it does what it did.
- `dash.RoleGrant` and `dash.AccessProfileRole` accept the three Workbench roles.
- A virtual directory named `workbench` is refused by the installer, as the other names of the site's own addresses are.
- The Workbench's database script checks the SQL Server certificate unless `-TrustServerCertificate` is given, as the
  dashboard's installer does.
- Under Entra sign-in with the Workbench on, the site asks for the operator's own token for the Power Platform
  inventory read, kept in the server's memory.

### Known limits
- **The Workbench on a real tenant and a real server.** Its worker service, the gMSA, the ledger digest task, the
  installer's new steps on IIS, ServiceNow, Teams and the Power Platform inventory were tested with stand-ins and the
  local test tenant only. Try it on a test server first.
- **One tenant.** On a site with several tenants the Workbench belongs to one (`Workbench:Tenant`, else the first).
- **Several web servers.** The operator's Power Platform token is kept per server: on another server they are asked to
  sign in again. Servers set up differently (one with the Workbench, one without) set the seat model in turn.
- **The worker's queue** keeps one small row per notice sent, and a notice whose handler stops the whole worker is
  tried again without end. A seat assigned directly with no license date in Entra waits `InactiveDays` before it can
  be proposed for reclaim.
- **Credit chargeback and Credit commitment** keep their environment routes; they do not use lines of business.
- **Licensing › Chargeback's *Charged to no group*** still opens Leavers with a different count, as in 2.7.7.

## [2.8.0] - 2026-10-28

Fewer grants to make by hand, and a second way in. A persona role can now be granted across the whole organization;
roles can be bundled into access profiles granted to groups as one, with a link to request each; grants can go to
Entra groups; and the dashboard can sign people in through Microsoft Entra ID instead of Windows. Windows sign-in stays
the default: a site that sets nothing new works exactly as before.

**Install over 2.7.7:** run `Install-CopilotAudit.ps1 -Dashboard` on the job server (three new tables and five new
columns, all additive), then build and deploy the dashboard from this release (docs\BUILD-FROM-SOURCE.md) on each web
server. The build needs these packages in the feed it uses, new in this release: `Microsoft.Identity.Web` 4.16.1,
`Azure.Identity` 1.21.0, `Azure.Extensions.AspNetCore.DataProtection.Blobs` 1.5.5,
`Azure.Extensions.AspNetCore.DataProtection.Keys` 1.6.5 and `Microsoft.ApplicationInsights.AspNetCore` 3.2.0, with
what they bring in. The next license tool run records each person's Entra object ID. To sign in through Entra ID, follow
docs\ENTRA-SIGN-IN.md; nothing else needs doing for Windows sign-in.

### Added
- **Admin › Access profiles.** A profile is a named bundle of roles, each with or without the whole organization, and
  Admin pages: grant it to a group, and whoever is in the group has the bundle; change it, and everyone who holds it has
  the change. The bundles people and groups hold today are offered as profiles in a click, optionally granted to their
  holders at once (their role-by-role grants are kept until removed), with four starters: Agent program lead, License
  manager, Security reviewer and Dashboard operator. Each profile can carry a request link, such as its Entra access
  package in My Access: anyone refused a page the profile would open is shown *Request <profile>*. Every change is
  audited with the profiles and their grants before and after; Power BI's *Organization* role counts Organization
  given through a profile.
- **A role across the whole organization.** Admin › Access › *Grant a role* has *Across the whole organization*: with a
  persona role (Adoption, Licensing, Security, Compliance, Agents, Enablement), that role's pages show the whole
  organization to its holder, where they showed the holder's own part. It widens that section only; the minimum group
  size and privacy mode apply as before.
- **Grants to Entra groups.** With the app registration in `Insights:Entra`, *Grant a role* and *Grant a profile* offer
  Entra groups by name. The grant keeps the group's object ID; membership, nested groups included, is checked through
  Microsoft Graph (`checkMemberGroups`, GroupMember.Read.All) at sign-in and kept ten minutes, whichever way people sign in.
- **Sign-in through Microsoft Entra ID** (`Insights:Authentication` = `Entra`; the IIS installer's `-Authentication
  Entra -EntraTenantId -EntraClientId -EntraCertificateThumbprint`). OpenID Connect with the authorization code and PKCE,
  a certificate or (on Azure) a managed identity as the app's credential, and *Sign out* in the header. A person is
  matched by their Entra object ID, then the on-premises SID the token can carry, then the UPN, which is refused when the
  directory records another account for that person. AD group grants keep working with Entra sign-in, from the members
  the nightly directory load records. An app role, `Insights.BootstrapAdmin`, makes administrators as
  `Insights:BootstrapAdmins` does. The data API takes a bearer token for the app's API. docs\ENTRA-SIGN-IN.md.
- **For Azure, off unless set:** the form keys in an Azure Storage blob protected with a Key Vault key
  (`Insights:DataProtection` = `Blob`), and Application Insights (`Insights:ApplicationInsightsConnectionString`).
- **The license tool records each person's Entra object ID** (`audit.CopilotLicense.EntraObjectId`, copied to
  `dash.Person.ObjectId` by the dashboard's refresh), with no new permission.

### Changed
- **Check someone's access** lists the roles that come through an access profile and through an Entra group (asked of
  Graph as the panel is drawn), and the sections the person sees across the whole organization.
- **The nightly directory load** also expands AD groups granted an access profile, and leaves Entra groups to the
  dashboard.
- **Admin has fifteen pages** to limit an administrator to, with Access profiles.

### Known limits
- **Entra ID was not tried against a real tenant.** Sign-in, the token's claims, the federated credential of a managed
  identity, Graph's answers for real groups, Key Vault, Blob Storage and Application Insights were built to Microsoft's
  documented contracts and tested with stand-ins only. Try it on a test site first, keeping a bootstrap administrator
  who can sign in with Windows on the production one.
- **Admin "view as"** (the plan's Phase 2) is not in this release.
- **The data API** keeps each viewer's own scope: a role across the whole organization widens that role's pages, not the API.
- **Licensing › Chargeback's *Charged to no group*** still opens Leavers with a different count, as in 2.7.7.

## [2.7.7] - 2026-10-28

A full rebuild of the report tables is fast again, no chart cuts a name short with "…", and Admin › Access ›
*Check someone's access* shows the roles a person holds through an AD group, not only those granted to them by name.

**Install over 2.7.6:** run `Install-CopilotAudit.ps1 -Dashboard` on the job server, as for 2.7.6 (the report procedure
`bi.usp_RefreshBi` changed; no table, column or view did), then build and deploy the dashboard from this release
(docs\BUILD-FROM-SOURCE.md) on each web server. The next nightly directory load records the members of every group
granted a role; until it has run, *Check someone's access* shows roles from Organization groups only.

### Changed
- **Check someone's access lists roles that come from groups.** Beside the roles granted to the account by name, it
  lists each role that reaches the person through an AD group, with the group's name, and covers them in what the
  person sees, whether they may open the dashboard and which Admin pages their Admin role covers. Before, it said
  "group grants are resolved when they sign in" and left the groups to be checked by hand. Group members are as of the
  nightly directory load; a group granted since then, or not found in AD, is named as having no members recorded.
- **The nightly directory load expands every group granted a role,** not only those granted Organization, into
  `audit.GroupMember` (`tools\Export-UsersWithHierarchy-ToSql.ps1`). Power BI's row-level security (`bi.OrgSecurity`)
  still gives the whole organization only to members of Organization groups.

### Fixed
- **A full rebuild of the report tables from empty takes 3.5 minutes on the demo, from 11** (211 s against 671 s, the
  demo built from 2.7.6 and from this release on the same PC): a month's accessed
  resources could be planned against a guess of one row from a small dimension, and then read the whole month's
  interactions once for every resource (about 3 billion rows). The month's interactions are now indexed by record,
  and a rebuild refreshes the small dimensions' statistics as each month adds to them.
- **A heatmap row name longer than its column wraps onto more lines** instead of being cut at 60 characters with "…";
  every row gets room for the most lines a name needs. Heatmaps whose names already fit draw as before.
- **A trend line whose name and value do not fit beside it** shows its value there and its name, whole, in the legend
  above the chart, as the forecast chart already did. Before, a long name was cut with "…". No chart cuts a name now.
- **Two packages with published vulnerabilities are updated:** `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Negotiate`, the
  Windows sign-in, from 10.0.12 to 10.0.14 (GHSA-vrrp-6v32-2p8g, high), and `System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs`, which
  it brought in at 10.0.0, now named at 10.0.14 (GHSA-846f-f764-76mx, high; GHSA-2fmv-rv2c-59x7, moderate). The build
  from source needs both versions in the package feed it uses.

### Known limits
- **Roles from groups were tested against the demo database and the SQL integration suite,** not against a real AD:
  nested groups, a group in a trusted domain and a large group were not tried with this release (the directory load's
  expansion is unchanged; only which groups it reads changed).
- **The rebuild's speed was measured on the demo,** not on the client's data. A rebuild over tables already filled
  took the same time with either release (105 s): the gain is in a rebuild whose small dimensions start empty.
- **Licensing › Chargeback's *Charged to no group* (61 on the demo) opens Leavers, which lists 57.** Chargeback also
  counts licensed accounts that are not in AD at all (guests, test and room accounts: 6 on the demo); Leavers lists
  disabled and departed accounts, and two disabled only in Entra. Unchanged from 2.7.6; those 6 are on the non-human
  accounts page.

## [2.7.6] - 2026-10-23

Ready for several web servers behind a load balancer, and for a virtual directory. The servers now share one report
cache through the database and build the pages once each morning between them; a load balancer has a health address to
probe; the site runs at an address such as https://apps.contoso.com/CopilotDashboard. Six pages that repeated others
are merged into the pages they repeated, a person's record charts their use, and an admin change is now audited in the
same transaction as the change, with what it changed. The nightly failure at License events is fixed.

**Install over 2.7.5:** run `Install-CopilotAudit.ps1 -Dashboard` (two new tables, `dash.QueryCacheShared` and
`dash.CacheGeneration`, a new column, `dash.AuditLog.Change`, and the wider `Operations` columns), then build and deploy
the dashboard from this release (docs\BUILD-FROM-SOURCE.md) on each web server. Nothing on the job server changes but
the scripts. Old addresses of the merged pages open the page that took them.

### Changed
- **Copilot on non-human accounts is one page,** listed in Licensing, Security and Compliance, where there were three
  copies; anyone with one of those roles opens it. `/security/non-human` and `/compliance/non-human` open it.
- **Agent inventory has *Shared* and *In production* views,** which were the pages Shared agents and Agents in
  production; `/agents/shared` and `/agents/production` open those views.
- **The Board pack takes in the Scorecard:** adoption split into Premium and free only, each unit one level down with
  its change, and a link to Value. `/leadership/scorecard` opens the Board pack.
- **Departments takes in the Leaderboard:** every department, division, country or office ranked against the period
  before, with the most improved; ranked by department, the change is a column of All departments rather than a second
  table of the same rows. `/adoption/leaderboard` opens Departments.
- **A report turned off before stays off.** In Admin › Reports shown, the non-human page is turned off section by
  section, as its three copies were, and the Scorecard, the Leaderboard, Shared agents and Agents in production are parts
  of the pages that took them, turned off as before: a switch set on 2.7.5 keeps its effect. The Board pack's units now
  show adoption only for a unit of at least the minimum group size of license holders.
- **Suite moves are no longer in the summaries.** The Costs and savings summary and What to act on no longer recommend
  moving people between E3, E5 and E7; Licensing › Suite fit still shows the analysis for whoever opens it.
- **A failure shows a reference, never the error's text,** to everyone, administrators included: "Not changed: it
  failed. Reference 3FA9C2: an administrator finds the details under it in the web server's log." The error, which can
  name servers, databases and accounts, is in the log under that reference. A refusal the dashboard makes itself (a
  value out of range, a line of a paste that does not read) still says what to correct.
- **The full reporting reference is attached to each release,** with both guides as Word documents
  (`REPORTING-REFERENCE.md`, `REPORTING-REFERENCE.docx`, `REPORTING.docx`). The repository keeps the reference's guide
  only, 1,459 lines where it held 18,256: Parts B and C were copies of `docs/SCHEMA.md` and of the scripts.
- **Code comments no longer carry release numbers** ("2.4.12: ", "(2.7.4)"): 974 comments in 172 files keep their
  explanation and drop the tag; CHANGELOG.md and the guides say when each thing came.

### Added
- **One report cache for every web server.** Each server keeps results in its own memory and, behind it, in the
  database: a page built on one server is fast on the others, a manager's part of the organization too, without session
  affinity. The morning build runs on one server at a time; the others wait for it and read what it kept. A result is
  kept under the data it was read from, so the nightly load or an administrator's change on any server makes every
  server read afresh, counted once the change commits. A result is shared only between servers running the same build,
  and only when it reads back as written; anything else stays on its server. A shared read or write waits at most two
  seconds on a lock, and old results are cleared 200 at a time, every half hour. Admin › Health shows what the servers
  share. `Insights:SharedQueryCache` (true) turns it off on a server.
- **`/healthz`, for a load balancer's probe:** `ok` when the server answers and reaches its (first tenant's) database,
  503 `unavailable` when it does not; GET or HEAD, over HTTP or HTTPS, no sign-in, nothing named. The installer lets that
  one address answer without Windows authentication.
- **A virtual directory.** `Install-CopilotInsights.ps1 -SiteName <site> -ApplicationPath /CopilotDashboard` installs
  the dashboard as an application inside an existing site, in an app pool and a folder of its own named after the path;
  every link, form, file and redirect carries the path. Behind a proxy other than IIS, `Insights:PathBase` sets it. The
  installer refuses a pool another site or application runs in, a folder holding files that are not the dashboard's, a
  path named as one of the dashboard's own addresses (`/admin`, `/agents`), and a run without `-ApplicationPath` on a
  site that holds the dashboard as an application.
- **A person's use over time** on their record: interactions and sessions a day (a week over 90 days), with links for
  7, 14, 30, 90, 180 and 365 days, days active and interactions a day active.
- **What an admin change changed.** An admin change and its audit row are written in one transaction: a change whose
  row cannot be written is not made. The row holds what was submitted (passwords, secrets, tokens, keys and webhook
  addresses masked, and any address's query, where a Teams or Logic Apps address keeps its signature) and the settings
  and role grants the change altered, before and after. Admin › Audit log shows it under *What changed*, as lines; its
  CSV has it as JSON. What runs long or reaches outside the database (a rebuild, retention, a test email or webhook,
  running the checks or an extract now, every tenant, the two uploads, taking a month again) is audited when it ends, as
  before, and a failure there says part of it may be done.
- **A test per audit loader against SQL Server:** each loader's operation set, taken from the nightly plan itself, is
  written where the loader records it (the backfill range, an incremental load and the CSV import) on a fresh schema.

### Fixed
- **The nightly stopped at License events** with "String or binary data would be truncated in table
  'audit.CopilotBackfillRange', column 'Operations'". 2.7.0 added the administrators' actions on agents to the
  license-event load, and its operation set, as recorded, grew from 382 to 485 characters, past the column's 400.
  `Operations` in audit.CopilotBackfillRange, audit.CopilotLoad and audit.CopilotCsvImport is now 2,000 characters,
  widened by the schema script every load runs first: deploying the scripts is enough, and the night resumes where it
  stopped. Until then, the same three `ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN Operations NVARCHAR(2000) NOT NULL` in the
  license-event database fix it by hand.
- **Adding a credit route** (Credit chargeback) left the list of routes as it was until the night's load: a write that
  returns a value was not counted as a change.
- **Copilot reservations with an empty register** showed every Microsoft 365 Copilot holder (17,886 at a client) under no
  listed leader, in red, with nothing to say why. It now says first that no organization is in the register yet, and
  where an administrator adds them and the rate.

### Known limits
- Three web servers were not run behind a load balancer here. Two dashboards on one database, side by side on this PC,
  gave the same 20 page views byte for byte as one without sharing, and the second built them in a quarter of the time;
  the morning lock was not raced between servers.
- The virtual directory was tried with `Insights:PathBase` under Kestrel, not with `-ApplicationPath` under IIS: the
  installer's new branch was not run on an IIS server. Bookmarks and email links from before need the path added.
- An adversarial review of the release found, and this release fixes: the webhook address unmasked in the audit record;
  running the checks now inside the change's transaction (a distributed-transaction error); reports turned off before
  the merge coming back; installer defaults that could share a pool or mirror over another site's folder; the shared
  cache's clean-up holding its table. Not changed: two admin changes saved in the same moment can deadlock, and one is
  then not made, with a reference; Admin › Email's SMTP failure text, shown to administrators, can name the mail server.
- Synthetic lab data, not the client's. Power BI Desktop: no `bi` view changed.

What a full review of every page and a stress test at 120 million interactions found, fixed: pages that rebuilt a view of
every person on each visit, queries that grouped every interaction by a name, tables with no download, summaries with no
headline, and two links that lost the whole-organization view. Measured on 120 million interactions and 210,000 people

### Changed

  four pages at 0.55 to 0.75 s from cache with no query run: the cost model, the credit estimate and suite fit built an
  object for every person from rows already kept, on every visit. They are now kept under the data's stamp, the period,
  the part of the organization and the versions of the tables that change during the day. From cache at 120M: What to

## [2.7.3] - 2026-10-21

The activity database's history no longer spends hours on a table nothing reads, and a database the installer
creates gets MAXDOP set for it. Then twenty passes over the dashboard: the slowest pages the first time they open,
figures that opened a page without their number, figures that said nothing of what they count, and the wording.

**Install over 2.7.2:** run `Install-CopilotAudit.ps1 -ActivityDatabase <name>` from this release; it replaces the merge
procedure. A history load already running finishes as it began. Then build and deploy the dashboard from this release
(docs\BUILD-FROM-SOURCE.md); nothing in its schema changes.

### Changed
- **Leadership › What to act on loads faster.** It read its six sources (the action counts, non-human accounts, units,
  targets, the cost figures and the security trend) one after another; it now reads them at the same time. On the demo
  data, a period not yet kept loads in 0.6–0.8 s instead of 0.9–1.2 s. Leadership › Overview, Organization and Apps
  and agents read their sources together in the same way.
- **Licensing › Swap list loads in a tenth of the time.** It read both sides (idle licenses and people wanting one)
  twice: once for the pairs and again for the four figures. One read now gives both; the figures are unchanged.
- **More pages read their sources together:** Security, Licensing, License overlap, Use cases and Scorecard. Their
  figures are unchanged; the gain shows on a large organization's data, where the reads overlap.
- **One separator between a section and its page.** Screens, mail and tips wrote both "Admin > Targets" and
  "Admin › Value names"; all now use ›, as the guides do.
- **Leadership › Apps and agents opens with figures:** interactions, the share in Copilot Chat and the share through
  an agent. Overview's Interactions opens it, and now finds the same number there.
- **Pages that were slowest the first time they open** (the demo data, a period not yet kept; the figures are unchanged,
  each compared with the previous build):
  - Governance › Copilot governance: 0.6–2.2 s to 0.25–0.45 s. Its seven reads start together, and Copilot by product
    classifies each person, app and agent once instead of every interaction.
  - Licensing › Credit use: 2.1–2.5 s to 0.25–0.3 s. The credit estimate grouped the interactions two ways at once
    with a distinct count, which read them twice and spooled them; one pass to a row per person and agent now gives
    the same rows. Agents costing credits, License for credits and Pay-as-you-go read the same estimate.
  - Enablement › Training effect: 1.1–1.8 s to 0.2–0.4 s, counting each person's active days in one range join on the
    day instead of two lookups a person.
  - Governance › AI apps, Apps and Enablement read their sources together; Enablement builds its population of
    licensed or active people once instead of three times.
- **Every headline figure says what it counts.** 41 figures on 17 pages had a label and a value and nothing else; each
  now has a note on the card or behind its information icon, and a test fails a new figure added without one.
- **Power users** (Enablement) and **Managers using Copilot** (Workforce) open the page that lists them.
- **Countries and offices' Highest and Lowest adoption** now say *Country with the highest (lowest) adoption*, beside
  the leaderboard's group of the same name.
- **Setup messages say who does what, the same way:** "An administrator sets this up by running
  Install-CopilotAudit.ps1 -Dashboard from <release> or later." Four told the reader to install a schema, one named an
  internal SQL file.

### Added
- **The installer sets MAXDOP on each database it creates**: the SQL Server's logical processors less two (at least 1),
  as a database-scoped configuration, so a large history's shred and the nightly refresh run in parallel and leave the
  server room. `-MaxDop <n>` sets it on every database it installs, existing ones included; `-MaxDop 0` leaves them
  all as they are. A database that exists keeps its own setting unless `-MaxDop` is given. Reading the processor count
  needs VIEW SERVER STATE; without it the installer says so and sets nothing.
- **`tools/dev/ui/Test-FigureLinks.ps1`**: opens the page behind each headline figure that is a link and checks it
  shows the same number, at as many periods as given. Part of the release checklist in `tools/dev/README.md`. On the
  demo data: 264 linked figures at six periods, none missing from its page; 26 lead on purpose to a related page in
  another month or unit (a month's credits to the people who used them) and are listed in the script.

### Fixed
- **An activity database's history spent hours building a table nothing reads.** Its `-Finalize` shredded every record's
  JSON into `audit.CopilotInteraction`, the Copilot reporting table, as a Copilot database's does. Nothing in the activity
  database reads that table: its records are shredded into their own tables by `audit.usp_ShredActivity`, which follows.
  At the client, 32 million records parsed at about 2 million an hour, which added roughly 16 hours to the history load.
  An activity database (one with `audit.usp_ShredActivity`) now leaves the table empty, at `-Finalize` and in each
  night's merge. The Copilot and license-event databases are unchanged.
- **Headline figures that opened a page without their number** (the rule since 2.6.7 is that a figure opens a page
  showing it):
  - Adoption's *Have started*, a share, opened the list of those who have not. That list's own count is now a figure
    of its own, from the same query, and carries the link.
  - Sensitive content's *People* counted those whose use touched labeled content; the list it opens also holds people
    only blocked from content (1,902 against 1,903 on the demo data). Both now count the same people, and the figure
    says so. *Blocked from content* now opens Security, whose *Blocked resources* is the same number.
  - Security's *Jailbreak attempts* and *Prompt injection detected* opened the flags of all three signals; each now
    opens the flags of its own kind.
  - Agents › Agents costing credits summed its estimate by agent, a few credits from Credit use's total that it opens;
    it now totals from people, as Credit use does.
- **Two chart labels left the chart on a phone:** a heatmap's row names (Drops and spikes) and a forecast line's end
  label (Forecast).
- **Licensing › Chargeback lost the licenses on disabled or missing accounts.** Its groups are enabled accounts found in
  the directory, so a license held by anyone else was paid for and charged to no group, and the page's total fell short
  of the licenses held (2,657 against 2,718 on the demo data). A figure, *Charged to no group*, now shows them with
  their monthly cost and opens Licensing › Leavers, which lists the same accounts. The total beside it is now named
  *Licenses charged to groups*.

### Known limits
- **Page times are the demo data's** (456,000 interactions on one SQL Server with 8 processors), cold, with no
  pre-cache. Each query rewritten for speed returns the same rows as before on the demo (compared in SQL and on the
  page at 7 to 365 days); the times at the client's 120 million interactions are not measured.
- **Not run at the client.** The activity shred's skip is proven by the SQL integration test and the source checks,
  not on the 32-million-record history; MAXDOP is set only on databases the installer creates, and only where its
  login holds VIEW SERVER STATE.
- **Power BI Desktop was not opened.** `powerbi/generate_model.py` writes the same model as 2.7.2; no `bi` view changed.
- Five figures lead on purpose to a related page that shows another month or unit (a month's credits to the people
  who used them, the seats to renew to the right size); `tools/dev/ui/Test-FigureLinks.ps1` lists them.

## [2.7.2] - 2026-10-20

Copilot Credits charged to each line of business, and a prepaid credit commitment tracked against its use: the
measurement a two-path Copilot Credit operating model (LoB Consumption and Enterprise Shared) and a Copilot Credit
Pre-Purchase Plan (P3) need.

**Install over 2.7.1:** run `Install-CopilotAudit.ps1 -Dashboard` from this release. It adds three tables
(`dash.CreditRoute`, `dash.CreditChargeSnapshot`, `dash.CreditCommitment`), one procedure and two settings; nothing else in
the schema changes. Then route the environments and record the commitment (docs\OPERATIONS.md, Copilot Credit chargeback
and commitment).

### Added
- **Leadership › Credit chargeback.**
  - Each line of business's Copilot Credits a month, by the path its environments are routed to: LoB Productivity, LoB
    Business Application, or Innovation. Enterprise Shared, and credits from environments not yet routed, are shown apart.
  - Each environment's credits, prepaid and pay-as-you-go, with what is charged at the charge rate and what Microsoft
    billed.
  - Exceptions: environments with no route, routes naming an Org ID not in Copilot reservations, and agents built by one
    line of business in another's environment.
  - Month-end snapshots: every complete month not yet kept, once the consumption report reaches its last day; never
    rewritten, except when an administrator takes a month again after routing its environments (audited).
  - For administrators: the routing register (one row at a time, or pasted from a spreadsheet, all checked first) and the
    charge rate.
- **Forecasting › Credit commitment.** A prepaid commitment such as the P3:
  - drawn, remaining and the burn rate;
  - when it runs out at that rate, or what it leaves unused;
  - drawn against an even plan;
  - the environments and lines of business drawing most.

  It is an estimate from the consumption report until Microsoft's applied figure is loaded.
- **An alert** when the commitment runs out, or is projected to, more than 30 days before its term ends, or to leave more
  than 30 days' worth unused, a commitment nothing draws on included (`CreditCommitmentAlertDays`, set on the page). It goes
  to `AlertLicensingTo`, once a week while it lasts. Terms may not overlap.
- Every figure on both pages says how it is worked out. Credit use, Agents costing credits, Copilot reservations and Costs
  and savings link to them. The charge rate and the warning days are in the assumptions register.

### Changed
- **The license cost of a period is whole calendar months** (Value and time saved, Board pack, the return on license
  cost). A period charges the calendar months whose last day falls inside it, each at the license price for everyone who
  held a license on at least one day of that month. So every figure is a multiple of the price (18, never 17.75 or 18.35),
  and the last 30 days charge one month. A period under a month charges none and shows no return. It was each day held
  at a 365th of a year. On the demo the 30-, 90- and 180-day costs move by +3.5%, +0.6% and −4.9%.
- Costs and savings no longer suggests buying Copilot Credit packs for metered credits while a commitment is in force:
  they draw on what is already paid for.
- The license pool alert names products, not part numbers.

### Fixed
- The operations guide said the activity database's history covered three record types; it covers those in
  `ActivityRecordTypes`, four by default.

### Known limits
- **Not run against the client's tenant.** An environment is matched to its route by the name the consumption report
  gives it. A billing policy that spans environments is entered on each of them.
- **The commitment's draw is an estimate**: the metered credits × what one credit draws. Microsoft's applied figure is
  in Azure Cost Management, which this release does not load.
- The wrong-environment check needs the agent inventory (its environment and owner) and a reservation register whose
  leaders cover the owners.

## [2.7.0] - 2026-10-20

An adversarial review of 2.6.7 and 2.6.8, and its fixes; usability from three people's walk through the dashboard; and
four more of Purview's records with the same app registration: administrators' actions on agents, Teams meeting AI
notes, data loss prevention matches where asked for, and Copilot by product.

To upgrade from 2.6.9: with the nightly task disabled, replace the job server's scripts, run
`Install-CopilotAudit.ps1 -SqlServer <server> -Dashboard` (with `-ActivityDatabase <name>` where there is one) once,
then install the dashboard package over the one in place and enable the task again. The installer adds two tables to
the Copilot database (`audit.ActivityUserDay`, `audit.DlpDay`) and one to the activity database (`audit.DlpMatch`);
nothing existing changes. From the next night, the license-event load also asks for the seven agent-management
operations, and the activity load for `TeamCopilotInteraction`: both from that night on. To load data loss prevention
matches, add `ComplianceDLPSharePoint` and `ComplianceDLPExchange` (and `DLPEndpoint` for devices) to
`ActivityRecordTypes` in the settings, beside the four defaults.

### Fixed (the review of 2.6.7 and 2.6.8)
- **Month-end snapshots showed the whole bank to every leader** on Leadership › Copilot reservations; they are now the
  viewer's organizations only, as a snapshot opened shows them. **Licensing › Reservation holders** is the viewer's part
  of the organization too: a Licensing holder of part of it listed every organization's people.
- **A changed reservation was counted twice**: a new row for an organization left its old one open, and the two were
  summed. A new row now ends the organization's open row the day before it starts; *End* ends a row on a day; a row that
  would overlap one starting on or after it is refused.
- **A pasted register was not all or nothing**: a bad line after good ones left the good ones added and the screen and
  audit log saying *Not changed*. Every line is now checked first (a quoted field may hold commas; a first line that is
  a row is not taken for the header), and the lines are added in one transaction. A database error in any admin
  change is now audited and said.
- **The month-end snapshot** waited for nothing: it is now taken once the licenses reach two days past the month end (a
  license change can reach Purview a day late), only when a reservation is in effect that day (a register entered ahead
  kept snapshots of the pools alone, for good), in one transaction, and not after a load the delete guard refused.
- **The reconciliation and purchase gate counted Copilot Studio's licenses and suites with Copilot** as add-on seats;
  they count the add-on only, as Costs and savings does.
- A leader who has left or whose account is disabled is now an exception (*Leader not in the directory*): the history
  of every user kept them as present. Removing a reservation or a rate is audited with what it was; a rate replaced says
  what it was before. Privacy mode names no leader. Obligations round half away from zero, so rows add up to the total;
  a rate shows as entered. Licenses on disabled accounts counts only those an organization counts.
- **The review of 2.7.0's own additions, before release:**
  - A new reservation row with an end date, inside a row that runs past it, is refused. Adding it ended the longer row
    the day before and left the organization with no reservation once the short one ended.
  - A rate takes at most two decimals, as it is kept.
  - *End on* has a field of its own and its own tip.
  - *Makers* on Build and publish no longer counts administrators who blocked or deployed an agent.
  - Who did an administrator's action is named only with the whole organization in view, since the panel is the organization's.
  - A field's tip is its page's where the same field name is used on several pages: App categories, digests' scope
    and the contracts' start had another page's text.
  - Copilot in Edge counts AppHost *Bing*, which is how Microsoft records Copilot in the Edge browser.

### Added
- **An information icon on every field of every form**: a setting's own description (without its release number), or
  a tip written for the field: the price list's volume price, Dataverse capacity, spare share and *bought for capacity*,
  the reservation register's fields, the resource map, targets, contracts, mail and alerts.
- **Agents › Build and publish › What administrators did to agents**: agents blocked, unblocked, deployed to people,
  removed, deleted or changed in the Microsoft 365 admin center, and the tenant's agent settings changed
  (`CopilotAgentManagement`), loaded with the license events in the same searches. Who did it: for the Agents role.
- **Teams meeting AI notes** (`TeamCopilotInteraction`), loaded by the activity database: the people using it beside
  Power BI and Power Apps on **Apps**, for any part of the organization (`audit.ActivityUserDay`).
- **Data loss prevention matches**, where the activity database is asked for the DLP record types: on **Compliance ›
  Sensitive content**, matches by workload over time and by policy, with those undone: overridden, no longer matching,
  or reported as a false positive (`audit.DlpMatch`, `audit.DlpDay`). Counts only: no file or message is named. Only a
  record that matched a policy is kept: a device's `DLPEndpoint` records also carry its ordinary file activity, audited
  with no rule matched, and those are left out; an endpoint's match is read from its `PolicyMatchInfo`.
- **Governance › Models and controls › Copilot by product**: Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Studio's and other agents,
  Security Copilot, Copilot in Fabric and Power BI, and Copilot in Edge and Bing, from the app each interaction names.
- **How figures are calculated › Copilot's cost a month, five ways**: what each of the five pages' Copilot cost counts,
  and which to quote for what.
- **Admin › Health › Next certificate to expire**, at the top.
- **Governance › AI apps beyond Copilot**: the Foundry accounts billed in the period with no call recorded.

### Changed
- Wording that ties figures counted different ways: *Unused for 30 days* (no use at all) against *Revoke* (no licensed
  use); the two train lists; *Revoke and reassign* (no new cost) against the Upgrade list (new licenses); billable
  against bought on Copilot reservations; the purchase gate against the spare seats. Plain words for the reservation
  figures. **Credit use** leads with what the admin center billed. A suite move to train shows what is at stake, apart
  from the savings. Admin labels: the Copilot price *after discount*, the pay-as-you-go cost with its currency, the
  Fabric discount *as a fraction*, *Idle after* for the Power Platform and AI accounts. Health no longer says no report
  reads the GitHub and Foundry tables.

### Known limits
- **Not run against the client's tenant.** The agent-management records' agent fields (`AgentId`, `AgentName`), Teams
  AI notes' and the DLP records' fields are read as Microsoft documents them; an endpoint match's `PolicyMatchInfo` is
  not yet seen in real records. Each record is kept whole: correct the shred and read them again.
- **The DLP record types are not loaded by default**: their volume is the tenant's every match. The record type for
  DLP of Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts is not documented yet.
- **Copilot by product groups by the app named**, not by each record's app identity, which bi does not keep: a product
  whose records name an app this does not know is counted as Microsoft 365 Copilot.
- The usability pass's remaining items are not in this release: product names in place of SKU part numbers, one
  renewal figure for Budget and renewal and License optimization, and the License inventory's bridge from bought to held.

## [2.6.9] - 2026-10-19

AI apps beyond Copilot, Power BI and Power Apps from the audit log, one place for every assumption, and savings that are
real. An optional **activity database** loads three more Purview record types with the same app registration and no new

calculated** lists every price and assumption a figure rests on and where it is set, and every money figure says how

To upgrade from 2.6.8: with the nightly task disabled, replace the job server's scripts, run
`Install-CopilotAudit.ps1 -SqlServer <server> -Dashboard` once, then install the dashboard package over the one in
place and enable the task again. The installer adds two tables, a function and a procedure to the Copilot database
(`audit.AIAppUserDay`, `audit.AIAppResource`, `audit.fnAIAppResourceGuess`, `audit.usp_RollupActivity`), six columns to
`dash.CostPrice` (volume price, Dataverse capacity a seat, spare share, bought for capacity; Power Apps Premium seeded at

nothing existing changes. Then, on Admin › Targets and assumptions, mark the licenses bought for capacity or the volume
price, and check the spare share. For the activity database, see *Added*.

### Added
- **The activity database** (optional; `docs/OPERATIONS.md`, *AI apps, Power BI and Power Apps*):
  - `Invoke-CopilotAuditBackfill.ps1 -RecordTypes` loads whole Purview record types; a database records them as
    `rt:<type>`, so it is never mixed with operations. Record-type searches are submitted to Graph's beta endpoint, whose
    list of record types has the newer ones.
  - `Install-CopilotAudit.ps1 -ActivityDatabase CopilotActivity` creates and installs it (`audit.AIAppCall`,
    `audit.PlatformActivity`, `audit.usp_ShredActivity`); it must be on the Copilot database's instance.
    `tools\Install-CopilotJobServer.ps1 -ActivityDatabase` saves it in the settings.
  - `Invoke-CopilotPipeline.ps1 -ActivityHistory` loads its history alone (180 days), finalized, shredded and rolled up;
    Copilot interactions are not loaded again. The nightly run then loads it after the Copilot load and rolls it up;
    both steps are optional and fail nothing else. `ActivityRecordTypes` in the settings replaces the three types.
  - `tools\Update-ActivityRollup.ps1` (`audit.usp_RollupActivity`) copies what the dashboard shows into the Copilot
    database, cutting days in the reporting time zone: AI app calls by day, resource, app, subscription and caller; the
    resources seen; and Power BI and Power Apps last active and active days in 30 (`audit.PowerPlatformUserActivity`,
    each product's rows replaced only when the activity database holds records of it).
- **Governance › AI apps beyond Copilot**: calls, conversations, resources, the share of calls without a user identity
  (an app calling with its own key), people (counted from the minimum group size, never named) and failures; calls over
  time with and without a person's identity; by line of business and environment; each resource with its Azure cost
  where the Foundry loader runs; departments calling with their own identity; and, for administrators, the resource
  map (line of business, environment and owner, guessed from names like `retail-prod-aif-0147` until set).
- **Leadership › How figures are calculated**: every price and assumption (49 on the demo) with its value, the
  figures that use it, who last changed it or *As installed*, and *Change it* for an administrator who may set it,
  which opens the page at the field; prices that disagree (the Copilot price in Access against the reservation rate
  in force and the contracts' price); and how each kind of figure is worked out.
- **How it is worked out**, under every money figure: on Costs and savings' tiles, Chargeback, License optimization,
  Budget and renewal, Rollout waves, License action outcomes, Fading use, Better with a license, Better on
  pay-as-you-go, Swap list, Credit use (the credit formula with its rates, and the token formula), Agents costing
  credits, Suite fit, Value and time saved and Copilot reservations: the formula with its values, then each assumption
  with its value and, for an administrator, *Change it*.
- **Prices that disagree** are said at the top of Costs and savings.

### Changed
- **Seat cuts are counted at what they really save** (Costs and savings):
  - **Spare seats kept on purpose** are not a saving: *Spare seats kept unassigned* (10% of those bought) for the
    Copilot add-on and every license, and a license's own share on its price row. 754 unassigned Copilot seats of
    18,640 are within the spare; nothing to cut.
  - **Bought for capacity or the volume price**: a price row's switch; its unassigned and idle seats are never money
    back (Power Apps Premium bought to 2,000 seats for its Dataverse capacity).
  - **The volume price**: the spend counts it, and a cut under it counts every seat going back to the list price, or
    stops at it where crossing it would save less.
  - **The Dataverse capacity a seat brings**: a cut that gives up more than the tenant has spare is less the add-on
    capacity it would need; without the capacity loaded, the saving is Low confidence and says it was not checked.
  - The monthly spend trend counts the volume price too.
- Chargeback's *Bought, not assigned* says what is beyond the seats kept spare.
- The installed settings include the pay-as-you-go cost of an interaction (0.12), which the pages assumed when unset.

### Fixed
- `Install-CopilotAudit.ps1 -ReportingTimeZone 'Eastern Standard Time'` on new, empty databases recorded nothing, as Eastern is the
  zone a database with none reads; the next install with no zone named then gave them the server's own zone (UTC on a
  server set to UTC). The zone named is now always recorded.

### Known limits
- **Not run against the client's tenant.** The three record types' fields are read as Microsoft documents them and as
  the client's two sample records showed (`AppIdentity`, `CopilotEventData.Contexts`, `Messages`, `ThreadId`,
  `AccessedResources`; Power BI's `ItemName` and `WorkSpaceName`; Power Apps' `AdditionalInfo`); the application name
  and subscription are read from three likely places each. Where one is named differently, correct the shred and read
  every record again (`EXEC audit.usp_ShredActivity;`): the records are kept whole. Submitting record-type searches to
  beta is untested against the live service; the stand-in accepts both endpoints.
- **Calls without a user identity cannot be tied to a person**, only to a resource and subscription.
- **The Dataverse check needs the capacity loaded** (`PowerPlatformCapacityDay`, by CSV until the Power Platform
  permission arrives). Fabric capacity, Copilot Credits and flow runs still come from CSV exports.
- Line of business and environment are guessed from resource names until an administrator sets them.

## [2.6.8] - 2026-10-19

Microsoft 365 Copilot reservations and chargeback: **Leadership › Copilot reservations** sets each line of business's
reserved seats against the add-on licenses its people hold, and shows what that bills, as the client's reservation
policy defines it: reserved, allocated, unused, over, billable, utilization and the monthly and remaining obligation by
organization, the reconciliation with the license pool, the purchase gate, exceptions to clear, and month-end snapshots
kept as they were. It is the current operational state, never certified; certification, adjustments, OIM intent and
the December close follow in later releases.

To upgrade from 2.6.7: with the nightly task disabled, replace the job server's scripts (the pipeline now keeps the
month-end snapshot), run `Install-CopilotAudit.ps1 -SqlServer <server> -Dashboard` once, then install the dashboard
package over the one in place and enable the task again. The installer adds four tables (`dash.Reservation`,
`dash.ReservationRate`, `dash.TechnologyAllocation`, `dash.ReservationSnapshot`), the function
`dash.fnReservationMember`, the procedure `dash.usp_TakeReservationSnapshot` and two settings; nothing existing
changes. Then, on Leadership › Copilot reservations, an administrator pastes the reservation register (Org ID,
organization, leader's sign-in, reserved, from), adds the rate (18 a license a month for 30 less 40%), sets the
purchase-gate baseline, and approves the Technology-funded accounts. The first snapshot is kept the next night.

### Added
- **Leadership › Copilot reservations.** For leaders, each seeing the organizations led from inside their part of the
  organization; the whole-organization view and the Licensing role see all.
  - A state line first: *Current operational state, not certified*, the day of the licenses read, and that billable
    licenses follow the policy's rule pending Finance's confirmation; or, for a snapshot, *Operational, not certified*
    and the day it was kept.
  - Figures: reserved; Entra allocated (the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on); unused reserved capacity (the sum of
    MAX(reserved − allocated, 0) by organization); allocation over reservation (the sum of MAX(allocated − reserved,
    0)); billable (reserved plus allocation over reservation); the monthly obligation (billable times the rate in force)
    and the remaining obligation (the months left in the year); add-on holders under no listed leader; the
    Technology-funded pool. Without a rate the obligations read *Pending Finance Decision*.
  - One row for each organization: Org ID, leader, cost center, reserved, allocated, unused, over, billable,
    utilization (N/A with nothing reserved), status (*Within*, *At* or *Over reservation*, *No reservation*, *Data
    exception*) and its monthly obligation, then those under no listed leader, the Technology pool and the total.
  - **Reconciliation and purchase gate**, for the whole organization: the add-on licenses bought, assigned and
    unassigned; the holders as counted here, and the difference to reconcile; the unused reserved capacity beside the
    unassigned inventory; and the purchase gate (no purchase until 95% of the baseline's unassigned licenses are
    assigned: at 1,136, 1,079, leaving a buffer of 57).
  - **Exceptions**: leaders not in the directory, a leader on two organizations, holders under no listed leader,
    non-human-looking accounts not in the Technology register, Technology allocations past their review date, licenses
    on disabled or departed accounts, and no rate in force; each with what to do and where.
  - **Month-end snapshots**, each kept once by the nightly run and never rewritten, with *View* to show one as it was.
  - For administrators: the **reservation register** (one at a time, or pasted from a spreadsheet, all checked before
    any is added), the **rate** by effective date, the **purchase gate**, and the **Technology-funded register**
    (account, category, accountable owner, approval reference, from and review dates). Every change is audited.
- **Licensing › Reservation holders**: the people an organization's allocated licenses count, those under no listed
  leader, or the Technology pool, with manager, licensed since and last use. For the Licensing role.
- `dash.usp_TakeReservationSnapshot`, run by the nightly pipeline after the licenses are read (a failure is logged and
  fails nothing), and `dash.fnReservationMember`.

### Known limits
- **Who counts where is a default**: an organization's people are everyone under its leader in the org chart, and a
  person under two listed leaders counts with the nearer one. A persistent chargeback hierarchy from another source, and
  cost-center mapping beyond the register's column, are not read.
- **Billable follows the policy's MAX(reserved, allocated) rule**, labeled pending Finance confirmation: the
  reserved-capacity proposal would bill on reservations alone. The purchase gate counts unassigned inventory; which pool
  it should count is Finance's to decide, and the unused reserved capacity is shown beside it.
- **Not yet built**: OIM approved intent, certification and sign-off, adjustments with approval lineage, recovery and
  overlap, true-down credits and new-reservation charges, the December close and the January chargeback output, and
  the masking of named users by role. Snapshots use the org chart of the night they were kept.
- **Tested on the demo database** (5,000 people, 15 reservations) and the SQL integration suite, not on the client's
  register or tenant.
- **A full bi rebuild can still take minutes on one month**, as in 2.6.6 and 2.6.7: its fix follows in its own release.

## [2.6.6] - 2026-10-19

One page for the whole AI and automation bill: **Leadership › Costs and savings** shows what Microsoft 365 Copilot,
Copilot Studio's credits, Fabric with Copilot in Power BI, Power BI, Power Automate, Power Apps with Dataverse, GitHub
Copilot and Foundry cost a month, what of it can be saved, and what it returns, with the savings ranked by what they

people, with its agents, guests, service accounts and a realistic six months of that spend.

To upgrade from 2.6.5: with the nightly task disabled, replace the job server's scripts, run
`Install-CopilotAudit.ps1 -SqlServer <server> -Dashboard` once, then install the dashboard package over the one in

### Added
- **Leadership › Costs and savings.** For whole-organization viewers and the Licensing role.
  - Laid out as a dashboard, the most important first and the cards two to a row, so it reads in about two screens;
    from 390 pixels wide to 1920, in the light theme and the dark.
  - *The headline:* one sentence (the spend, its return, and what taking the savings would do), then five tiles: the
